fields.description: Turn this on to enable the scheduled LinkedIn Posts Scraper. Leave off until Auth is configured and tested.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: Cookie auth reuses a session you already established by logging in normally in your own browser - lower risk of triggering LinkedIn's security checkpoint than a fresh automated login from a server.
fields.label: Authentication Method

fields.description: The value of the "li_at" cookie from a browser where you're already logged into LinkedIn (DevTools → Application/Storage → Cookies → linkedin.com → li_at). Expires periodically and will need refreshing.
fields.label: li_at Cookie Value

fields.description: Higher risk of triggering LinkedIn's security checkpoint/CAPTCHA when logging in from a server IP. Prefer Cookie auth if possible.
fields.label: LinkedIn Email

fields.description: Maximum posts to fetch per Competitor on each scheduled run.
fields.label: Posts per Competitor

fields.description: Uses a free, open-source LLM running locally via Ollama to label each new post (New Client, Publicity & Marketing, New Technology, etc). If Ollama isn't reachable, posts are just left unclassified - scraping itself is unaffected.
fields.label: Enable AI Classification

fields.description: Base URL of the Ollama server.
fields.label: Ollama Host

fields.description: Must already be pulled on the Ollama server (ollama pull <model>).
fields.label: Ollama Model

fields.options:
Scraping LinkedIn is against their Terms of Service. Using an account for automated scraping carries a real risk of that account being restricted or banned - use an account you're comfortable with that risk on, not a primary personal or company account.

The scheduled job runs daily and only scrapes Competitors that have a LinkedIn Company URL set.
